| `ollama` | on your machine, through an Ollama server | only vectors reach Qdrant. `--embedding-url` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (`OSTLER_EMBEDDING_URL`); set `--embedding-model` and `--embedding-dim` to match the model. Remote plain-`http` embedders are refused |
| `dev-hash` | on your machine, deterministic hash | **not semantic.** Exact-key and `autocomplete` lookups work; fuzzy meaning does not. For open-source Qdrant development |

Exact signals need no vectors: lookups by playbook mapping and `autocomplete` token use payload filters.

## Transport

Plain `http://` to a non-loopback Qdrant is **refused**, because the API key and facts would cross the network unencrypted. `--allow-insecure-qdrant` (`OSTLER_ALLOW_INSECURE_QDRANT`) overrides it for links already protected by a VPN or tunnel. **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.**

If Qdrant fails twice in a row (transport error or 5xx), lookups are skipped for 30 seconds and tool results start with `Note: memory is unavailable (...); continuing without it.` Requests time out after 4 seconds.

## Per-tenant access tokens

By default all tenants share three collections, separated by a `tenant` filter in every query. A leaked **admin key** exposes every tenant in that mode. For stronger separation: **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.**

- `--isolation collection` gives each tenant its own collections.
- `ostler memory token` mints a **JWT that Qdrant itself limits** to those collections, read-write or `--read-only`, and expiring. A leaked client token then exposes one tenant, not the cluster.
- Qdrant must run with `service.jwt_rbac: true`, and an admin must create the collections first.

```sh
# 1. as admin: create alice's collections (`ostler memory list` does it)
export QDRANT_URL=https://<cluster>.cloud.qdrant.io:6333 QDRANT_API_KEY=<admin key>
export OSTLER_ISOLATION=collection OSTLER_TENANT=alice
ostler memory list

# 2. mint a token for alice (30 days by default; add --read-only for search-only)
ostler memory token --days 30

# 3. give alice the token instead of the admin key
#    QDRANT_API_KEY=<token>  with  --isolation collection --tenant alice
```

Tested on a real Qdrant 1.20: another tenant's collections answer 403, and expired, forged and read-only tokens are refused. Qdrant 1.20 rejects the older per-point `payload` claim as deprecated, so isolation is **per collection**.

Not covered: the default `shared` isolation shares collections, so a leaked admin key exposes every tenant, and collection isolation needs `jwt_rbac` and an admin who creates the collections. Over [A2A](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html), all conversations share one tenant; run one server per tenant if callers must not see each other's profile.

## How retrieval works

For a field, in order of reliability:

1. the form's own **playbook** mapping;
2. an exact `autocomplete`-token match against your facts (payload filter, no vectors);
3. a **playbook from a similar form on the same site** (a redesign or sibling form);
4. semantic vector search.

`form_fill` with `auto: "required"` fills what memory can supply and reports the rest. Semantic matches need a margin over the runner-up and never apply to labels about other people. Playbooks persist only exact (playbook or `autocomplete`) matches.

## It learns from every fill

Ostler needs no model to judge whether a fill worked: the browser reads every value back and the page accepts or rejects the submit, so every outcome is ground truth.

| step | what happens | Qdrant feature |
|---|---|---|
| recall | exact form first; after a redesign, mappings transfer from a similar form on the same site with the same label | keyword-array filter on `labels_norm` and `host`, tenant index |
| rank | proven, recently verified skills beat stale or failing ones | Query API prefetch and a **score-boosting formula** (similarity, smoothed win rate and `exp_decay` on `verified_ts`) |
| reinforce | verified fields on accepted submits add wins per mapping | integer payload indexes |
| demote | a mapping that loses more than it wins is dropped | |
| forget | `ostler memory prune --days 90` removes stale, unproven skills; `serve` also forgets those not verified for 180 days on start (`--retain-days`, 0 keeps them). Saved facts never expire | range filter on `verified_ts` |

On a scripted site with redesigned forms, correct suggestions went from 1 to 8 of 10 fillable fields, with zero wrong fills in both conditions. That is a synthetic fixture, not real sites ([ADR-0008](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-learning-loop.md)).

## Commands

```sh
ostler memory list                      # saved facts
ostler memory remember email you@example.com
ostler memory forget email
ostler memory skills                    # what was learned: wins, losses, trusted mappings
ostler memory prune --days 90
ostler memory seal                      # re-save pre-sealing memory sealed
ostler memory key export --yes-print    # back up the sealing key
ostler memory token                     # per-tenant JWT (see above)
ostler memory wipe --yes                # delete everything for this tenant
```

No Qdrant? `ostler init --local` (or `ostler config set memory local`) keeps memory in one file, `memory.local`, next to your config. It survives restarts, needs no server, and the whole file is encrypted with the same memory key as sealed Qdrant memory (AES-256-GCM, written atomically, safe to use from `serve` and `ostler memory` at once). Embeddings stay on your machine: local word hashing by default (finds shared words, not meaning), or `--embeddings ollama` for semantic search. Back up the key; lost, the file cannot be read. `--seal off` stores plain JSON instead.

Just trying things out: `ostler memory --memory ephemeral list` keeps memory in-process and loses it on exit.

## Which keys do I need?

| you want | you need |
|---|---|
| browsing and form filling only | nothing |
| memory, no server, kept across sessions | `ostler init --local` (encrypted file on this machine), no keys |
| memory, trying it out | `--memory ephemeral` (in-process, lost on exit), no keys |
| memory on **Qdrant Cloud** | cluster URL and API key, with **Inference enabled** on the cluster |
| memory on self-hosted Qdrant | URL (plus key if you set one) and `--embeddings dev-hash`, or `--embeddings ollama` for semantic search |

See [Security model](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/security.html) for the threat-model rows on secrets, cross-user exposure and anyone who can read your Qdrant.

### Upgrading older memory

Two kinds of older sealed points need one command, `ostler memory seal`, which is safe to repeat and copies before it deletes:

- **`v1` blobs** (written by early builds) are no longer read: they did not authenticate the clear fields. `serve`, `memory list` and the other commands stop with the command to run; the upgrade opens them once with your key and saves them as `v2`.
- **Keys saved under an older normalisation** (emoji-only keys, decomposed accents) sit at a different point than today's lookup asks for. The same command re-files them under the current key and removes the stray copy, without overwriting a newer fact.

On Linux, `key_store = keychain` needs a running Secret Service (gnome-keyring, KWallet). Without one Ostler stops with the reason and `ostler config set key_store file`; it never falls back by itself, so the key is never half in a keyring and half on disk.


---

Source: https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/configuration.html

# Configuration and CLI

Settings come from, in order: **command-line flag, then environment variable, then the config file, then the default.** One path per setting, so what `ostler serve` does is what `ostler doctor` tested.

## Easy setup

```sh
ostler init
```

Asks for a Qdrant URL and API key (skip both for no memory), a tenant name, and whether to enable `--learn` and `--lean`. It writes the config file with owner-only permissions and immediately tests the connection. Non-interactively:

```sh
ostler init --qdrant-url https://<cluster>.cloud.qdrant.io --qdrant-api-key "$KEY" --tenant alice
```

The `:6333` port is added to Qdrant Cloud URLs for you. If the connection test fails the settings are still saved, so you can fix one value instead of retyping everything:

```sh
ostler config show                          # key is masked
ostler config set qdrant_url http://localhost:6333
ostler config unset learn
ostler config path                          # ~/.config/ostler/config.toml
```

## Config file reference

`~/.config/ostler/config.toml` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or the path in `OSTLER_CONFIG`):

| key | environment variable | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `qdrant_url` | `QDRANT_URL` | Qdrant REST endpoint |
| `qdrant_api_key` | `QDRANT_API_KEY` | Qdrant API key (secret; file is `0600`) |
| `tenant` | `OSTLER_TENANT` | isolates users sharing a cluster (default `default`) |
| `memory` | `OSTLER_MEMORY` | `auto` (on if a URL is set), `qdrant`, `local` (encrypted file, no server), `ephemeral`, `off` |
| `embeddings` | `OSTLER_EMBEDDINGS` | `cloud` (Qdrant Cloud Inference), `ollama` (local) or `dev-hash` |
| `embedding_model` | `OSTLER_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Cloud Inference model (default `sentence-transformers/all-minilm-l6-v2`, 384 dims) |
| `qdrant_on_disk` | `OSTLER_QDRANT_ON_DISK` | keep vectors on disk: less RAM per user |
| `learn` | `OSTLER_LEARN` | save non-sensitive values typed after an accepted submit (off by default) |
| `lean` | `OSTLER_LEAN` | lower memory use; no images in screenshots |
| `tools` | `OSTLER_TOOLS` | `core`, `forms` or `all` |

Other environment variables used by the code: `OSTLER_SEAL`, `OSTLER_ISOLATION`, `OSTLER_MEMORY_KEY`, `OSTLER_EMBEDDING_URL`, `OSTLER_EMBEDDING_DIM`, `OSTLER_ALLOW_INSECURE_QDRANT`, `OSTLER_RETAIN_DAYS`, `OSTLER_KEY_STORE`, `OSTLER_ALLOW_NEW_KEY` (same as `--allow-new-key`: let a first start create the sealing key while Qdrant cannot be checked), `OSTLER_VERBOSE`, `OSTLER_CHROME`, `OSTLER_NO_SANDBOX`, `OSTLER_A2A_BIND` and `OSTLER_A2A_TOKEN`. The seal, isolation, embedding-URL, insecure-Qdrant and retention settings are **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.**.

## Commands

```text
ostler <COMMAND>

  serve      Run the MCP server on stdio (what the agent launches)
  a2a        Serve Agent2Agent (A2A) over HTTP so other agents can delegate forms
  init       Guided setup: Qdrant URL/key, tenant, privacy choices (sealing, local embeddings, retention); then verify
  config     show | path | set <key> <value> | unset <key>
  setup      Print or apply the config for claude | codex | cursor | vscode | json
  doctor     Check that Chrome launches, and report memory: Qdrant reachable, sealing, key, embeddings, isolation, transport
  inspect    Open a URL and print the typed form model as JSON
  memory     list | skills | prune --days N | remember <key> <value> | forget <key> | seal | key export/import | token | wipe --yes
  fixtures   Serve the demo form pages (default port 8787)
```

`ostler memory` also has `seal` and `token` **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.**, described in [Memory and privacy](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/memory.html). Memory flags go before the subcommand: `ostler memory --memory ephemeral list`.

## `ostler serve` flags

| flag | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--tools` | `auto` | `auto` lists the core tools and adds forms and memory when a page has form fields; or `core`, `forms`, `all` |
| `--lean` | off | lean Chrome flags; no image, font or media downloads |
| `--headed` | off | show the browser window |
| `--profile-dir DIR` | throwaway | persistent Chrome profile (keeps logins); one profile per server |
| `--chrome-path PATH` | auto | Chrome binary (`OSTLER_CHROME`) |
| `--allow-domain D` | any | only this domain and subdomains; repeatable; `D:8443` pins a port |
| `--allow-file` | off | permit `file://` URLs |
| `--upload-dir DIR` | none (uploads refused) | directory file fields may be filled from; repeatable |
| `--block-private-networks` | off (`a2a`: on) | with no allowlist, refuse loopback, private, metadata and internal hosts (`a2a --allow-private-networks` opts out) |
| `--accept-dialogs` | off | answer the page's `confirm()` and `prompt()` with OK (dismissed by default) |
| `--require-confirm-submit` | off | `form_submit` needs `confirm=true` |
| `--learn` | off | save non-sensitive typed values after an accepted submit |
| `--verbose` | off | timings, fingerprints and ids in tool output (costs context) |
| `--memory` | `auto` | `auto`, `qdrant`, `local`, `ephemeral`, `off` |
| `--qdrant-url`, `--qdrant-api-key` | none | Qdrant endpoint and key |
| `--embeddings` | `cloud` | `cloud`, `ollama` (embed locally, only vectors leave) or `dev-hash` |
| `--embedding-model`, `--embedding-dim` | MiniLM, 384 | embedding model and its dimension |
| `--embedding-url` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | where the Ollama embedding server lives **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.** |
| `--qdrant-on-disk` | off | vectors on disk |
| `--seal` | `auto` | encrypt memory on this machine before it reaches Qdrant (`on`, `off`) **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.** |
| `--isolation` | `shared` | `collection`: one set of collections per tenant, pairs with `ostler memory token` **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.** |
| `--allow-insecure-qdrant` | off | allow plain http to a non-loopback Qdrant **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.** |
| `--retain-days` | 180 | forget unverified skills and episodes on start (0 = keep) **Unreleased: main branch, not a tagged release.** |
| `--tenant` | `default` | memory namespace |

Set `OSTLER_NO_SANDBOX=1` to run Chrome without its sandbox (needed as root or in some containers). See [Troubleshooting](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/troubleshooting.html).

## `ostler a2a` flags

`ostler a2a` takes the same flags as `serve`, plus:

| flag | default | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--bind` | `127.0.0.1:8765` | address to listen on. Anything other than loopback requires `--a2a-token` |
| `--a2a-token` | none | bearer token clients must send (`OSTLER_A2A_TOKEN`) |
| `--public-url` | none | externally visible base URL for the Agent Card |
| `--allowed-host` | none | additional accepted `Host` header values; repeatable |
| `--max-contexts` | 4 | concurrent remote conversations; each one is a Chrome process |
| `--idle-secs` | 300 | close a conversation's browser after this many idle seconds |
| `--a2a-auto-submit` | off | treat `submit: true` as already confirmed |

See [A2A](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html) for the protocol and its security notes.


---

Source: https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/tools.html

# Tools reference

Ostler exposes 32 MCP tools in five profiles. `--tools auto|core|forms|research|all` (or `OSTLER_TOOLS`) controls how many the agent sees. The default, `auto`, starts with the 16 core tools (4.9 KB of schema), adds the research tools after the first `read` or `search`, and adds the form and memory tools once a page shows form fields. The server sends `tools/list_changed`, the result names the new tools, and every tool stays callable even if a client never refreshes its list. The full set is about 9.7 KB of schema, roughly 2.7k tokens on every turn, and a test keeps it under 11 KB. Tool output is terse by default (verified fields are named once, no timings or fingerprints); `--verbose` brings the debug detail back.

| profile | tools | count |
|---|---|---:|
| `auto` (default) | core, growing to research, forms and memory as the session needs them | 15 to 30 |
| `core` | browse, `read`, tabs and context tools | 15 |
| `forms` | core plus the form tools | 19 |
| `research` | core plus the research tools | 21 |
| `all` | everything, including memory and `stats` | 30 |

Page-derived text in results (page content, titles, URLs, dialog text, the `look` legend) is wrapped in `<page_content untrusted="true">`. The server instructions tell the model not to follow it. See [Security model](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/security.html).

## Browse (profile: core)

### `navigate`

Open a URL. Returns page state with interactive elements, so no separate snapshot call is needed.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string, **required** | |
| `observe` | `interactive` \| `full` \| `none` | default `interactive` |

It reports the HTTP status (`Navigated (HTTP 404)`) with a plain-language reason, labels PDFs, downloads and redirects to a sign-in page, and explains navigation errors. A CAPTCHA or "verify you are human" page produces a `CHALLENGE:` line at the top. On a search-results URL whose visible text matches fewer than about half of the query's words, it adds a `Warning: results do not seem to match the query`.

### `snapshot`

Read the page as text with element refs (`e1`, `e2`, …). Use delta to see only changes. Pass the ref of a heading to read just that section.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `full` \| `delta` \| `interactive` | |
| `ref` | string | limit to a subtree |
| `max_chars` | integer | |

Long text is split into several lines with an explicit `… [N more chars cut]` marker. Text a person cannot see is left out and counted.

### `read`

Read a page for research (opens `url` if given). With `query`: only the best passages, ranked locally with BM25 and MMR, so a page costs a few hundred tokens instead of the whole text. Without: the start of the page. Only pages read this session can be cited.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | opens it first; omit to read the current tab |
| `query` | string | what you are looking for |
| `k` | integer | passages, default 5, max 12 |
| `max_chars` | integer | default 8000 |

The header names the page, its size, fetch time and content hash, and flags what a reader must know first: `PAYWALL`, `CHANGED` (the page differs from an earlier read; earlier citations from it are re-checked), the page's own paging text (`showing 1-5 of 13`), and `ATTENTION` when the page contains text aimed at an AI. A bot wall, robots.txt refusal, HTTP error or empty page is `NOT READ` and is recorded as a gap, never as a source.

### `click`

Click an element by ref. The result ends with a `Result:` line: navigated, popup opened as tab `tN`, page updated, or no visible change.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string, **required** | |
| `observe` | `delta` \| `full` \| `none` | default `delta` |

### `hover`

Move the pointer over an element by ref (opens menus and tooltips).

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string, **required** | |
| `observe` | `delta` \| `full` \| `none` | default `delta` |

### `scroll`

Scroll an element into view (`ref`) or the page (`direction`). Reports the position as scrolled/max, so the agent knows when it has reached the end of an infinite list.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string | element to bring into view |
| `direction` | `up` \| `down` \| `top` \| `bottom` | |
| `amount` | integer | pixels |
| `observe` | `delta` \| `full` \| `none` | default `delta` |

### `type`

Type into an element by ref, replacing its content.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string, **required** | |
| `text` | string, **required** | |
| `submit` | boolean | press Enter after |
| `observe` | `delta` \| `full` \| `none` | default `delta` |

### `press`

Press a key, for example `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `Control+a`.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string, **required** | |
| `observe` | `delta` \| `full` \| `none` | default `delta` |

### `wait_for`

Wait until text appears or disappears, or a CSS selector shows, or just pause for `ms` milliseconds (max 10000).

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | wait for it to appear |
| `text_gone` | string | wait for it to disappear |
| `selector` | string | CSS selector |
| `timeout_ms` | integer | |
| `ms` | integer | plain pause |

### `wait_for_human`

A CAPTCHA or verification wall is blocking the page: wait for the user to complete it in the browser window. Needs `--headed`. Ostler never solves these itself.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout_s` | integer | default 120, max 600 |

### `screenshot`

Capture a PNG of the page or one element.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string | one element |
| `full_page` | boolean | |

### `look`

See where to click: a screenshot with every clickable element boxed and numbered by its ref, plus a legend saying what each does (type here, submits the form, error, …). Use the refs with `click`, `type` and `fill_field`.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `max` | integer | |

Boxes come from DOM geometry and are coloured by role: green submits, blue inputs, purple links, red has an error. Elements hidden under a cookie banner, modal or sticky bar are left out and counted, so the agent closes the overlay first. It covers only the visible viewport. The overlay is removed afterwards. With `--lean`, screenshots omit images.

### `back`

Go back in history. Takes no parameters. At the start of a tab's history it says so instead of landing on `about:blank`.

## Tabs and shared notes (profile: core)

### `tabs`

Manage tabs. They share cookies and the `context` tool. Popups open as new tabs.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `list` \| `new` \| `switch` \| `close`, **required** | |
| `tab` | string | tab id, for example `t2` |
| `url` | string | for `new` |

### `search_tools`

Find Ostler tools without listing them all: names, one-line descriptions or full input schemas for any tool, listed or not.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | words that must appear in the name or description |
| `detail` | string | `names`, `brief` (default) or `full` |

### `context`

Notes shared by every tab and later calls: `get`, `set`, `delete`, `list`. Keep short facts, not page dumps. Survives a browser restart.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | `get` \| `set` \| `delete` \| `list`, **required** | |
| `key` | string | |
| `value` | string | |

## Research (profile: research)

Built around one contract: **an answer can only contain what was read and verified.** See the [Cookbook](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/cookbook.html#13-research-with-citations-that-are-checked) for the workflow.

### `cite`

Check a quote against a page read this session. `VERIFIED` returns the page's exact words and a `#:~:text=` link a person can open to check them. `NOT READ` (the page was never read), `NOT VERIFIED` (with the closest text on the page) and `TOO SHORT` are errors: do not use that claim. Markdown on either side is ignored, so `**1887**` and `[Marta Ilves](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/m)` still verify.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | string, **required** | a page read with `read` or `open_many` |
| `quote` | string, **required** | words from the page, 12+ characters; `...` marks an omission |

### `evidence`

What the agent has read and may state: verified citations, citations made stale by a changed page, pages read but not cited, and the gaps (paywall, bot wall, robots.txt, HTTP error, empty page). Call it before answering. Takes no parameters.

### `search`

Web search through SearXNG (`OSTLER_SEARXNG_URL`) or Brave (`OSTLER_SEARCH_PROVIDER=brave` and `OSTLER_BRAVE_API_KEY`). Returns titles, URLs and snippets; a snippet is not evidence until the page is read.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, **required** | |
| `limit` | integer | default 8, max 20 |
| `recency` | `day` \| `week` \| `month` \| `year` | |
| `site` | string | host name, for example `example.com` |

### `open_many`

Read up to 10 URLs in a scratch tab; the agent's current tab is untouched. The domain policy is checked before robots.txt is fetched, robots.txt (RFC 9309) is obeyed, requests to one host are spaced, and the call has a time budget. Each page's outcome is reported.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `urls` | string array, **required** | |
| `query` | string | best passages from each page |
| `k` | integer | passages per page, default 2, max 5 |
| `force` | boolean | re-read pages already read |

### `extract`

Structured data from the current page: `tables` as rows, or `lists` of repeated cards with pagination hints and a completeness verdict (`PARTIAL: 5 of 13` when the page states a total it does not show).

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `tables` \| `lists`, **required** | |
| `max_rows` | integer | per table or list, default 30 |
| `where` | string | keep only rows containing any of `a\|b\|c` |
| `select` | array | table columns to keep, by header name or index |

### `links`

Links on the current page with anchor text and context, optionally filtered.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `same_origin` | boolean | |
| `text_contains` | string | |
| `href_contains` | string | |
| `limit` | integer | default 30 |
| `where` | string | keep only lines containing any of `a\|b\|c` |

### `run`

Run a short [Rhai](https://rhai.rs) script for multi-page jobs. Loops, filtering and counting happen outside the context; only the script's printed lines and final value come back, inside the untrusted fence. In the script, `tool("read", #{url: u, query: "price"})` runs any Ostler tool and returns its text; `grep(text, word)`, `lines(text)` and `print(x)` help. No files, network, modules or `eval`; at most 60 tool calls; every call keeps the profile, allowlist, robots.txt and submit-gate rules, and `run` cannot call `run`. See [ADR-0019](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0019-scripted-runs-and-result-filtering.md).

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `script` | string | required |
| `max_chars` | integer | default 8000 |

## Forms (profile: forms)

### `form_inspect`

List the page's forms as typed fields (label, kind, required, options, errors) plus submit controls and what memory knows about this form.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `form` | string | form ref |

### `form_fill`

A value written `{{fact:KEY}}` is replaced by the saved fact with that key, so the value never has to pass through the agent. An unknown key fails the call.

Fill many fields at once from `{label | name | ref: value}`. Handles selects, radios, checkbox groups, dates, files, comboboxes and dependent dropdowns, and verifies each field by reading it back. `auto: "required"` or `"all"` fills the rest from memory.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | object | `{label \| name \| ref: value}` |
| `form` | string | form ref |
| `auto` | `off` \| `required` \| `all` | fill the rest from memory |
| `min_confidence` | number | |

The report names each field `OK`, or says `UNMATCHED` (no field matches the key), `ambiguous` (several match equally well, so use the ref), or a read-back mismatch. It lists fields still empty and required, and says `unsettled` (a count) when the page was still busy at the end of the fill. File fields are refused unless `--upload-dir` allows the directory.

### `form_submit`

Click the form's submit or next control and report whether it was accepted, advanced to another step, or failed validation.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `form` | string | |
| `control` | string | submit button ref |
| `confirm` | boolean | required when the server runs with `--require-confirm-submit` |

Result: `Submitted`, `Advanced` (next step), `NOT ACCEPTED` with the page's own messages, or `Nothing changed` when the form stays put and says nothing. Just before clicking it re-reads the fields it verified and reports any the page cleared or rewrote (`CHANGED BEFORE SUBMIT`).

### `fill_field`

Set one field by ref (any kind, including custom widgets).

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ref` | string, **required** | |
| `value` | any, **required** | |

## Memory (profile: all)

These need memory enabled (`--memory local`, a Qdrant URL, or `--memory ephemeral`). See [Memory and privacy](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/memory.html).

### `memory_remember`

Save a fact about the user for future forms (for example email, company). Secrets are refused.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string, **required** | |
| `value` | any, **required** | |
| `description` | string | |
| `autocomplete` | string | HTML autocomplete token, for example `given-name` |

### `memory_recall`

Semantic search over saved facts.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | string, **required** | |
| `limit` | integer | |

### `memory_list`

List all saved facts. Takes no parameters.

### `memory_forget`

Delete a saved fact by key.

| parameter | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string, **required** | |

### `stats`

Session cost and latency counters: calls, milliseconds, estimated tokens, browser memory. Takes no parameters.

## Design notes

- **Observation is part of the action.** `navigate` returns the interactive elements; clicks and typing return only what changed. `observe: none` opts out but still records a baseline.
- **Actions are never replayed after a navigation.** Calls that change the page report that the page changed instead of re-running.
- **A crashed Chrome is relaunched** and the agent is told. Open tabs and page state are lost.


---

Source: https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/security.html

# Security

Ostler lets an AI agent drive a real browser and stores some user data. Treat it like any tool that can act on your behalf.

## Supported versions

Pre-1.0: only the latest released minor version (currently 0.2.x) and `main` receive security fixes.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting for this repository ("Security" tab → "Report a vulnerability"). Do not open a public issue for something exploitable. There is no bounty. This is a pre-1.0 project maintained by individuals.

Include the version, how you ran it (flags, transport), and a minimal reproduction. What to expect, on a best-effort basis:

1. We acknowledge the report as quickly as we can.
2. We confirm and assess the impact, and tell you if we disagree it is a vulnerability.
3. We prepare a fix privately, release it, and publish an advisory crediting you unless you prefer otherwise.
4. Please keep the details private until a fix is released; we ask for coordinated disclosure and will not rush you if you need time either.

## Automated supply-chain checks

The `Security` workflow (`.github/workflows/security.yml`) runs on every push to `main`, every pull request and weekly:

- `cargo deny` with [deny.toml](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/deny.toml): RustSec advisories and yanked crates, an allow-list of licenses, wildcard version requirements, and sources (crates.io only; no git dependencies). Duplicate versions of a crate are reported as warnings, not failures.
- `cargo audit --deny warnings`: `Cargo.lock` against the RustSec database, including unmaintained and unsound warnings.
- Dependabot (`.github/dependabot.yml`) opens weekly grouped updates for Cargo dependencies and GitHub Actions.

These cover known-vulnerable and disallowed dependencies. They do not detect unknown vulnerabilities, malicious but unreported crates, or flaws in Ostler's own code. Workflows use read-only tokens, do not use `pull_request_target`, and pin actions by tag, not by commit SHA.

## Threat model

| threat | what we do | what we do not do |
|---|---|---|
| **Prompt injection from a web page** | Page-derived text is wrapped in `<page_content untrusted="true">`: page content, but also titles, URLs, dialog text and the `look` legend, which used to sit on trusted lines. Text a person cannot see (opacity 0, zero font size, far off-screen, same colour as the background) is left out and counted, so a hidden instruction never reaches the model. Server instructions tell the model not to follow page text. | We cannot stop a model from being persuaded by text a person can also see. Hidden-text detection judges colour only against a solid background; gradients, images and `clip`-style screen-reader text are not treated as hidden. Use `--allow-domain` and `--require-confirm-submit` for anything sensitive. |
| **Agent navigates somewhere it should not** | Domain allowlist enforced inside the browser. Every request the page makes is held and checked whatever its type (documents, images, stylesheets, scripts, `fetch`/XHR, beacons, event streams), and Chrome is started with a resolver rule that makes every other host unresolvable, which also covers WebSockets and the first request of a popup. Entries may pin a port (`example.com:8443`). Only http(s); `file:` needs `--allow-file`. Tested with a canary server on a non-allowlisted origin: no request arrives through `<img>`, a stylesheet, `fetch`, XHR, a beacon, a WebSocket, `EventSource`, a form POST, a redirect, a meta refresh, a script navigation or `window.open`, by hostname or by IP literal. With no allowlist, `--block-private-networks` refuses loopback, private, link-local (cloud metadata), CGNAT and internal-looking hosts, and names that resolve to them. Independently of that flag, navigating to a literal link-local address (169.254.0.0/16 including 169.254.169.254, `fe80::/10`, `fd00:ec2::254`) or a well-known metadata hostname (`metadata.google.internal`) is refused unless you allowlist it. | An entry without a port allows every port on that host. Ports are checked on the requests interception sees; the browser-wide resolver rule works on hosts only, so treat a port pin as defence in depth, not isolation, for WebSockets. The private-network check resolves a name before Chrome does, so a DNS-rebinding server can answer differently the second time: use an allowlist where that matters. `--block-private-networks` is off by default for `serve` because coding agents browse local dev servers (and the demo fixtures live on loopback); it is on by default for `a2a`. The always-on metadata check covers navigations and literal addresses only: without an allowlist, a page's own sub-requests and names that merely resolve to a metadata address are not checked. Not a sandbox against a compromised browser. |
| **Irreversible submissions** | `--require-confirm-submit` blocks every non-GET request unless it happens inside `form_submit` with `confirm=true`. | Off by default. A GET with side effects, and WebSockets, are not covered. The first request of a popup window and requests from cross-site iframes (their own browser processes) are covered too: Chrome is told to hold such targets at start (`Target.setAutoAttach` with `waitForDebuggerOnStart`) and interception is switched on before they are released, so `--allow-domain host:port` pins and the gate apply to them (tested with a canary: popup POST, popup GET to another port, cross-site iframe POST/`fetch`/image). A submit that is cancelled mid-flight now closes the gate again. At most 8 popups are adopted (the rest are closed before they run). A popup opened by the form you confirmed inherits the confirmation for its first request only, so a hostile page that opens a window during a confirmed submit can let that popup's first request through. |
| **File exfiltration through an upload field** | File fields are refused unless you pass `--upload-dir DIR`. A path is resolved first (`..` and symlinks included) and must land inside an allowed directory; the browser is handed the resolved path. | Anything inside an allowed directory can be attached to any page the agent visits, so keep it small and free of secrets. |
| **A page's own "are you sure?" dialog** | `confirm()` and `prompt()` are dismissed, so a site's "Delete everything?" is not confirmed by a browser nobody is watching, and the agent is told what happened. `alert()` and `beforeunload` are acknowledged. | `--accept-dialogs` restores auto-accept for sites that need it. A dismissed confirm can leave a flow stuck; the agent sees the dialog text and can ask you. |
| **A remote agent over A2A** | Loopback by default; bearer token required to listen elsewhere; `Origin` and `Host` checks against browser-based attacks; per-conversation browsers; submit needs an explicit confirm; private and internal addresses are refused unless you pass `--allow-private-networks`. | No TLS (use a reverse proxy). All conversations share one memory tenant. Always pass `--allow-domain`. See [docs/A2A.md](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html). |
| **Secrets in memory** | The memory API refuses password/token/card-like keys and card-number-like values; sensitive fields are never auto-filled from memory nor stored by `--learn`; sensitive values are masked in tool output; playbooks store structure only, never values. | Detection is heuristic (names, `autocomplete` tokens, digit patterns). A secret stored under an innocuous key with an innocuous value will not be caught. |
| **Cross-user data exposure** | Every memory point carries a `tenant`; every query filters on it; isolation is tested on a real Qdrant. With `--isolation collection` each tenant has its own collections and `ostler memory token` mints a JWT Qdrant itself limits to them (tested on Qdrant 1.20: other tenants answer 403). | The default shares collections, so a leaked admin key exposes every tenant. Collection isolation needs `jwt_rbac` and an admin who creates the collections. |
| **Someone who can read your Qdrant (operator, leaked key, backup)** | Payloads are sealed on your machine (AES-256-GCM); site names, labels, keys and point ids are keyed hashes; episodes are redacted of emails and numbers; plain `http://` to a remote Qdrant is refused. | The vector is not hidden: with `--embeddings cloud` the field text is sent to Qdrant Cloud Inference, and vectors of labels reveal roughly what they say. Use `--embeddings ollama` to keep text local. Tenant name, win/loss counters, timing and point counts stay visible. The key is a file or env var by default (optionally the macOS Keychain or Linux Secret Service via `key_store = keychain`). Lose it and sealed memory is unreadable; `serve` refuses to start rather than silently replace a key that cannot open existing memory, and a first start only creates a key after Qdrant was seen to hold no sealed memory for the tenant (with Qdrant unreachable it refuses unless you pass `--allow-new-key`). Sealed blobs in the old `v1` format are not read (run `ostler memory seal` once to upgrade them). Two simultaneous first starts on the Linux keychain are serialised by a lock file, which does not cover other programs writing the same Secret Service item; that path is tested against a scripted fake `secret-tool`, not a real keyring. |
| **Malicious page attacking the runtime** | The injected runtime avoids `eval` and never executes page-supplied strings; it works on DOM objects. It runs before page scripts and keeps its own references to `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest` and `setTimeout`. | The runtime shares a JS world with the page, so a hostile page can replace `window.__wm`, patch `Element.prototype` / `Array.prototype` / `JSON` / `Map` after load, or read the runtime's functions, and so mislead what the agent is told (a field's value, whether something is visible or required) or how long a fill waits. Running it in a CDP isolated world was investigated and is **not** done: the activity tracking that settle depends on works by patching `fetch`, XHR and timers in the page's own world, which an isolated world cannot do, and the same-origin-iframe walk calls the other frame's `__wm`. Doing it needs a split into a small main-world tracker and an isolated-world runtime ([ADR-0004](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-injected-runtime.md)). Page DOM content itself is always attacker-controlled; do not rely on the runtime for adversarial pages. |
| **Local exposure** | Chrome is launched with a throwaway profile and talks to Ostler over a pipe (`--remote-debugging-pipe`). There is no debugging port, so no other local user can connect to the browser, and Chrome exits by itself if Ostler dies. Tested: no listening socket in the browser's process tree (the WebSocket mode shows one). | `OSTLER_CDP_TRANSPORT=ws` brings back the old unauthenticated localhost port, for debugging only. With `--profile-dir` your logged-in sessions live on disk, readable by your own account and by any process running as you. |

Not audited. No security review has been done by a third party.

## Verify it yourself

Each claim above has a test that runs against a real Chrome (`OSTLER_REQUIRE_CHROME=1` makes a missing Chrome a failure instead of a skip):

```sh
OSTLER_REQUIRE_CHROME=1 cargo test -p ostler-browser --test security_e2e   # allowlist canary, uploads, dialogs, ports, private networks
OSTLER_REQUIRE_CHROME=1 cargo test -p ostler --test mcp_e2e page_text_never_reaches_a_trusted_line
OSTLER_REQUIRE_CHROME=1 cargo test -p ostler-browser --test forms_e2e text_a_person_cannot_see
OSTLER_REQUIRE_CHROME=1 cargo test -p ostler-cdp --test no_debug_port        # no listening socket
cargo test -p ostler-browser --lib policy                                     # URL, port, private-range and upload-path rules
```

The allowlist test puts a canary server on a host outside the allowlist and loads a page that tries to reach it through an image, a stylesheet, `fetch`, XHR, a beacon, a WebSocket, `EventSource`, a form POST, a redirect, a meta refresh, a script navigation and `window.open`. A control run with no allowlist must reach the canary, so "nothing arrived" cannot be a broken test. The allowlist, screenshot and trust-boundary (`page_text_never_reaches_a_trusted_line`) tests were run against the code before their fixes and failed there. The upload, dialog, port, private-network and debugging-port tests pair each protection with its opt-out or a control run, so they cannot pass by testing nothing.

## What is stored, where

- Qdrant (your cluster): facts you saved, form playbooks (field labels and which fact filled them), episodes (error messages from forms), all tagged with your tenant. By default these are encrypted before upload (`--seal`); the key is `memory.key` beside your config file or `OSTLER_MEMORY_KEY`.
- Disk: nothing by default; a Chrome profile only if you pass `--profile-dir`.
- Telemetry: none.

`ostler memory wipe --yes` deletes everything for a tenant.


---

Source: https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html

# Agent2Agent (A2A)

Ostler can be driven by another agent over [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org) (v1.0, JSON-RPC over HTTP, SSE streaming), as well as by a coding agent over MCP. Use MCP when one agent owns the browser; use A2A when another agent (or service) should be able to hand Ostler a form as a task.

```sh
ostler a2a --allow-domain example.com          # http://127.0.0.1:8765
curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/.well-known/agent-card.json
```

Ostler is a **tool, not a language model**. It understands structured requests, not free text. It tells a client so (it answers chatter with a message that shows the expected shape).

## Sending work

Send `SendMessage` (or `SendStreamingMessage`) with a `data` part:

```json
{"url": "https://example.com/signup",
 "values": {"Email": "ada@example.com", "Country": "Germany"},
 "submit": true}
```

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | page to open first. Omit to continue on the conversation's current page |
| `values` | `{label \| name \| ref: value}`, filled and verified by reading each field back |
| `auto` | `required` or `all`: fill the rest from the owner's saved profile (needs Qdrant memory) |
| `submit` | submit once everything is filled and verified |
| `confirm` | the caller agrees to the submission |

No `values`, no `auto`, no `submit`: it just **inspects** the form. A bare URL in a text part does the same.

## The task lifecycle

| state | when | what the client does |
|---|---|---|
| `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` | inspected, filled, or submitted and accepted | read the artifacts |
| `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED` | required fields missing, a key matched nothing or was ambiguous, the page rejected a value, a wizard advanced, or it is **waiting for `{"confirm": true}`** | reply on the same `taskId` with more `values` or `confirm` |
| `TASK_STATE_FAILED` | blocked by policy, timed out, or the page never accepted the submit | read the `result` artifact |
| `TASK_STATE_CANCELED` | `CancelTask` | |

**Nothing is submitted until the caller says `confirm: true`**, unless the server runs with `--a2a-auto-submit`. A remote agent can of course just send it; the point is that a human-in-the-loop client has a place to stop.

Each task has two artifacts: `result` (compact text) and `data` (the same information as JSON: `missing`, `unmatched`, `fieldErrors`, …). Both are marked `metadata.untrusted: true` because they contain text from the website. Treat them as data, never as instructions.

## Conversations share state

One A2A `contextId` is one Ostler session: its own Chrome, its own **tabs**, and its own shared **context** notes. Messages with the same `contextId` (or the same `taskId`) continue where the last one stopped, e.g. the form that was filled is still open when `{"confirm": true}` arrives. Different `contextId`s can never see each other's pages.

Each conversation is a Chrome process (about 400-650 MiB), so it is capped: `--max-contexts` (default 4), idle ones are closed after `--idle-secs` (default 300).

## Methods

`SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SubscribeToTask`. `GetExtendedAgentCard` and the push-notification methods return the A2A errors for "not supported" (`-32007`, `-32003`). Errors use the A2A codes (`-32001` task not found, `-32002` not cancelable, `-32004` unsupported operation, `-32009` version not supported) with a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` detail.

`A2A-Version` must be `1.x` if sent. A missing header is accepted (the spec says to assume 0.3, which this server does not implement, so being lenient here is a deliberate choice).

## Limits, timeouts and shutdown

The HTTP front door is bounded so a slow, greedy or abusive client cannot exhaust the machine. These are fields of `A2aConfig` (defaults shown). Only those with a flag shown have one today; the rest are library defaults until `ostler a2a` exposes them.

| Setting (`A2aConfig`) | Default | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_body_bytes` | 1 MiB | Larger request bodies get HTTP **413** (checked against `Content-Length`, and while reading chunked bodies). |
| `header_read_timeout` | 10 s | Time to send a request's headers; also the idle limit on a kept-alive connection. The connection is closed on expiry (slowloris). |
| `body_timeout` | 15 s | Time to send the body once headers are in. HTTP **408** on expiry. |
| `request_timeout` | 150 s | Ceiling on handling a request until its response starts (SSE streams continue afterwards). Raised to `task_timeout + 15 s` if lower, so a blocking `SendMessage` is never cut short. HTTP **408**. |
| `max_concurrent_tasks` | 8 | Tasks running, or queued behind their conversation's turn. Over the limit: HTTP **429**, `Retry-After: 5`, error reason `TOO_MANY_TASKS_IN_FLIGHT`. Nothing is queued without bound. |
| `max_contexts` (`--max-contexts`) | 4 | Concurrent conversations (one Chrome each). Over the limit: HTTP **503**, `Retry-After: 15`, reason `TOO_MANY_CONTEXTS`. |
| `task_timeout` (`--task-timeout-secs`) | 120 s | One task; it then fails with "The task timed out." |
| `idle` (`--idle-secs`) | 300 s | Idle conversations are closed. |
| `drain_timeout` | 30 s | See shutdown below. |

429/503 responses are JSON-RPC errors (code `-32603`) with `error.data[0].metadata.retryAfterSeconds`, plus the `Retry-After` header. Clients should back off and retry.

**Probes** (no auth, no `Host` check, body is only a status word; nothing about the host, paths or versions):

- `GET /healthz`: `200 {"status":"ok"}` while the process is serving.
- `GET /readyz`: `200 {"status":"ready"}` when the server is not shutting down and a Chrome binary can be found (`chrome_path`, else the usual discovery order); otherwise `503 {"status":"not_ready"}`. It checks that a browser can be located, not that a launch succeeds.

**Request ids.** Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header. A client-supplied `X-Request-Id` (up to 64 characters of `A-Za-z0-9-_.`) is echoed; otherwise a UUID is generated. Error bodies repeat it: `requestId` in the plain-JSON auth/host/timeout errors and `error.data[0].metadata.requestId` in JSON-RPC errors. Quote it when reporting a problem.

**Graceful shutdown.** On SIGTERM or SIGINT the server stops accepting connections, `/readyz` turns 503, new tasks are refused with 503 (`SHUTTING_DOWN`), and in-flight requests and tasks get up to `drain_timeout` to finish. Anything still running is then aborted, every browser is closed, and the process exits. Set your orchestrator's termination grace period above `drain_timeout`.

Not limited here: the number of open connections. Put a reverse proxy or firewall in front for connection-level limits.

## Securing it

An A2A endpoint lets a network client steer a browser that can log in to things. Defaults are conservative:

- Binds **127.0.0.1**. Binding anything else **requires `--a2a-token`** (or `OSTLER_A2A_TOKEN`); the server refuses to start otherwise.
- With a token, the RPC endpoint needs `Authorization: Bearer …` (compared in constant time). The Agent Card stays public, as the protocol expects, and advertises the scheme but never the token.
- Requests carrying an `Origin` header (a web page in a browser) are refused, and the `Host` header must be a loopback name or one you list with `--allowed-host`/`--public-url`. This blocks drive-by and DNS-rebinding attacks from a page open on the same machine.
- **Always set `--allow-domain`.** Without it, any remote agent can send this browser to any public website. The allowlist is enforced inside the browser for every conversation (every request type, WebSockets included). Without an allowlist the server blocks loopback, private and cloud-metadata addresses so a remote agent cannot probe this machine's network (`--allow-private-networks` turns that off); the server warns at startup. Uploads are refused unless you pass `--upload-dir`.
- TLS is not terminated here. Put it behind a reverse proxy for anything beyond localhost, and set `--public-url`.
- All conversations share one Qdrant `tenant`. If different callers must not see each other's saved profile, run one server per tenant.

## Verified against

The official A2A Python SDK (`a2a-sdk` 1.3.0) resolved the card, selected the JSON-RPC interface, streamed a three-turn conversation (input-required, input-required, completed) and received artifacts on every turn against the real binary. That was a manual check; the repository's own tests (`crates/ostler-a2a/tests`) use plain HTTP.

Not implemented: gRPC and REST bindings, push notifications, extended cards, signed cards, and the v0.3 wire format.


---

Source: https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/architecture.html

# Architecture

```
  agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …)
        │  MCP / JSON-RPC over stdio
        ▼
  ostler-mcp ── tool catalogue, profiles, safety gates, metrics, memory glue
        │                                  │
        ▼                                  ▼
  ostler-browser                  ostler-memory ──► Qdrant (REST)
   Page / fill engine / snapshots      profile · playbooks · episodes
                                       (sealed on this machine by default)
        │         │
        │         └─ ostler-forms (form IR, key→field matching, value normalisation)
        ▼
  ostler-cdp ── async CDP over a pipe to Chrome (WebSocket optional), Chrome launcher
        ▼
  Chrome (headless by default, --headed to show the window)  ◄── runtime.js injected into every document
```

| crate | responsibility |
|---|---|
| `ostler-cdp` | One connection to the browser (a `--remote-debugging-pipe` by default, so there is no listening port; `OSTLER_CDP_TRANSPORT=ws` for debugging), id-matched requests, broadcast events, flattened target sessions, Chrome discovery/launch, process-tree memory measurement. No browser-automation dependency. |
| `ostler-browser` | `Page` (navigate, snapshot, click, type, key, upload, screenshot, wait), the fill/verify/submit engine, domain policy, the in-page runtime. |
| `ostler-forms` | Pure logic, no I/O: form IR types, matching agent keys to fields, option/date/time normalisation, sensitive-field detection, form fingerprints. |
| `ostler-memory` | `Store` trait with `QdrantStore` (Cloud Inference or client vectors from a local embedder: Ollama or the non-semantic hash), `InMemoryStore` and `SealedStore` (client-side encryption wrapper); `Memory` API for one tenant; per-tenant Qdrant access tokens (`token.rs`). |
| `ostler-mcp` | JSON-RPC loop, 32 tools in 5 profiles (16 core, 20 forms, 23 research, 32 all; `auto` grows from core), lazy browser, per-tool metrics, background memory writes. `evidence.rs` holds the research session: pages read (markdown for passages, plain words for verification), verified citations, re-verification when a page changes; `app/research.rs` wires `read`, `cite`, `evidence`, `search`, `open_many`, `extract` and `links` to `ostler-browser`, `ostler-extract` and `ostler-research`. |
| `ostler-a2a` | The Agent2Agent HTTP surface (`ostler a2a`); see [A2A.md](https://inamdarmihir.github.io/ostler/docs/a2a.html). |
| `ostler` (`crates/ostler-cli`) | `serve`, `a2a`, `init`, `config`, `setup`, `doctor`, `inspect`, `memory`, `fixtures`. |
| `ostler-fixtures` | The 49 form test pages (`PAGES` in `crates/ostler-fixtures/src/lib.rs`, plus an internal 404 page), the domain packs under `packs/` (research, gov-forms, jobs, dev-qa, commerce: 34 tasks, 29 pages), and a recording HTTP server (`/__records`, `/__reset`, `/exfil`, `/pay`, `robots.txt`, a second origin port). |
| `ostler-bench` | Forms / footprint / concurrency / memory-scale benchmarks and the LLM cost model. |

## The decisions that matter, and why

Each has an ADR in [`docs/adr/`](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/tree/main/docs/adr) where the alternatives are written down.

**An injected runtime instead of CDP's accessibility tree.** A single script (`runtime.js`) runs inside every document and does traversal, snapshotting and field manipulation. It sees open shadow roots and same-origin iframes through one code path, can run React-safe native setters, and answers a question in one round-trip that would take dozens of CDP calls. The cost: it is our code running in a hostile page's world, so it is written defensively (no `eval`, no page-supplied selectors executed as code) and it cannot see closed shadow roots or cross-origin frames.

**A form IR, not form primitives.** `form_inspect` returns typed fields (kind, label, required, options, pattern, current value, error) and submit controls. `form_fill` takes `{label | name | ref: value}`, resolves each key to a field (exact ref → name/id → label → fuzzy; **ambiguity is reported, never guessed**), normalises the value for the field (option text → option index, `"March 5, 2001"` → `2001-03-05`, `"3:30 PM"` → `15:30`; ambiguous `03/04/2024` is refused), fills in document order, **re-inspects after every field** so dependent controls appear, and **reads each value back**. This is what removes round-trips: the model states intent once.

**Settle by counting work, not by sleeping.** Page scripts are wrapped so the runtime knows how many `fetch`/XHR requests and short timers are in flight. After any action it waits until the DOM is quiet *and* nothing is pending. Fixed sleeps are either too short (flaky) or too long (slow). The wrapper must not count its own polling; getting that wrong cost us 3 s per action until the benchmark exposed it.

**Verification with a fallback strategy.** Typed input (`Input.insertText`) is tried first because it fires the same events a user would. If the page rejects it (masked or framework-controlled inputs), the engine retries with the native value setter plus events. Values the page reformats (`(555) 123-4567`) are reported as *reformatted*, not as errors.

**Submit outcomes.** `form_submit` classifies the result as `ValidationFailed`, `Advanced` (next wizard step), `Submitted`, `Unchanged` or `ServerError`. `ServerError` is an HTTP 4xx/5xx answer to the submit with no validation messages on the page: it is reported as failed, never as submitted, and the agent is told the data may or may not have been stored. With no `form` argument, `submit` targets the form that `form_fill` last filled (`last_form`, cleared after every submit); if the page has several forms and none was filled, it refuses and lists them rather than guessing the first.

**Observation is part of the action.** `navigate` returns an interactive snapshot; `click`/`type`/`press` return a delta snapshot. Saves a tool call per step and keeps the context small. `observe: none` opts out.

**Memory as three kinds, one tenant filter.** *Profile* (facts about the user), *playbooks* (structure of forms that worked: field labels and which fact fed them, **never values**), *episodes* (validation errors and failures, deduplicated with a count). Retrieval prefers the most reliable signal first: the form's own playbook mapping → the field's `autocomplete` token matched against facts (payload filter, no vectors) → a trusted mapping from a similar form on the same host, ranked in Qdrant by a score-boosting formula over similarity, win rate and recency → semantic vector search. Every fill outcome patches the playbook: wins reinforce a mapping, failures demote it, and `prune` forgets stale, unproven skills ([ADR-0008](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-learning-loop.md)). Writes happen in the background, never on the response path. Every point carries `tenant`, indexed with `is_tenant`; `--isolation collection` instead gives each tenant its own three collections (the usual names prefixed with `ostler_<tenant>_`), see "Tenant tokens" below. On start, `serve` forgets learned skills and episodes not verified for `--retain-days` (default 180; 0 keeps them); facts you saved never expire.

**One Qdrant API, three vector sources (`--embeddings`).** `cloud`: with Qdrant Cloud Inference the client sends `{text, model}` and Qdrant embeds server-side, so the field text reaches Qdrant. `ollama`: a local Ollama server embeds on this machine (`--embedding-url`, default `http://127.0.0.1:11434`) and only vectors reach Qdrant; plain http to a non-loopback embedder is refused. `dev-hash`: a deterministic client-side hash embedder for tests and open-source Qdrant development; explicitly **not** semantic.

**Sealing (`SealedStore`, `--seal auto|on|off`).** With memory in Qdrant, `auto` wraps the store so Qdrant never sees plaintext payloads. Per point: `tenant`, `wins`, `losses` and `verified_ts` stay in clear (Qdrant filters, ranks and expires on them); `key_norm`, `fingerprint`, `autocomplete`, `id_hint`, `host` and `labels_norm` become keyed hashes (HMAC-SHA-256), so equality filters still work without the server learning site names, labels or keys; everything else (fact values, descriptions, playbooks, episodes) is AES-256-GCM encrypted with the point id bound in as associated data, so a blob moved to another point does not open and a point that fails to open is skipped. **Point ids are keyed**: unsealed ids are a UUIDv5 of tenant, kind and key (guessable: anyone could test `uuid5(tenant, "profile", "passport number")`), sealed ids are derived with the index key. Both sub-keys come from one 32-byte master key (`OSTLER_MEMORY_KEY`, or an owner-only `memory.key` beside the config file, created on first use). Not hidden: the vector, the tenant name, win/loss counters, timing and point counts. Lose the key and sealed memory is unreadable (`ostler memory wipe --yes` starts over). `ostler memory seal` migrates facts saved before sealing; learned skills and episodes from then are dropped and relearned. It also upgrades `v1` blobs (not read by this build: `v2` authenticates the clear fields) and re-files facts and playbooks whose lookup key predates the current `norm()`; `probe_key` reports both as `NeedsUpgrade`, and every start refuses until `memory seal` has run. The key is created only on a first start in which Qdrant was seen to hold no sealed memory for the tenant (`--allow-new-key` covers a first-time setup with Qdrant down), under a lock file for the keychain store. Episodes are additionally redacted of emails, runs of 4+ digits and URL query strings before they are embedded or stored. Plain `http://` to a non-loopback Qdrant is refused unless `--allow-insecure-qdrant`.

**Tenant tokens.** With `--isolation collection`, each tenant gets its own collections and `ostler memory token` mints an HS256 JWT, signed with the Qdrant admin key, whose `access` claim limits the bearer to those collections (optionally read-only, 30 days by default). It needs Qdrant with `service.jwt_rbac: true`. Isolation is per collection because Qdrant 1.20 rejects the older per-point payload-filter claim.

**Safety is structural.** With an allowlist, every request the browser makes (documents, sub-resources, WebSockets, popups) is held and checked, and Chrome is started with a host-resolver rule that makes every other host unresolvable. Without one, navigations are checked and cloud-metadata addresses are always refused; loopback and LAN stay open so local dev servers work (`--block-private-networks` closes them). Non-http(s) schemes are blocked; `--require-confirm-submit` blocks every non-GET request outside a confirmed submit (`submit` arms the gate for its own duration through a `Disarm` drop guard, so a cancelled or timed-out submit, e.g. an A2A deadline, cannot leave the page able to send data); secrets are refused by the memory API and never auto-filled; sensitive values are masked in reports, snapshots and notes; page-derived text (including titles and URLs) is wrapped in `<page_content untrusted="true">` and the server instructions tell the model not to follow it. If Qdrant fails twice in a row, lookups are skipped for 30 s and tool results say so.

## Known limits (deliberately not hidden)

- Chrome/Chromium only (Lightpanda/other CDP engines are a planned pluggable backend, see ADR-0001; not implemented).
- Cross-origin iframes and closed shadow roots are invisible to the runtime.
- No CAPTCHA solving, 2FA, anti-bot evasion or login-state management beyond `--profile-dir`. Verification walls are *detected and handed to a person* (`CHALLENGE:` notice, `wait_for_human`, A2A `input-required`); this is deliberate, see [ADR-0009](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-challenges-are-handed-off.md).
- Calendar pickers on read-only inputs are handled heuristically (month header, prev/next, day cells); dropdown-only and year-only pickers are not.
- MCP runs over stdio only; `ostler a2a` is the HTTP surface.
- Linux and Windows are untested locally; CI covers Linux and Windows (Windows is experimental).

## Related

[SYSTEM-DESIGN.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/SYSTEM-DESIGN.md) (context, constraints, capacity, trade-offs) · [THREAT-MODEL.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md) · [FAILURE-MODES.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/FAILURE-MODES.md) · [SLOS.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/SLOS.md) · [COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [OPERATIONS.md](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/OPERATIONS.md) · [ADR-0011](https://github.com/inamdarmihir/ostler/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-reliability-principles.md)
